dietEvidence.body: The curved, serrated teeth indicate carnivory. No gut contents are known, so the prey taken, hunting versus scavenging, and feeding frequency remain unknown.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A small early tyrannosauroid with preserved filamentous integument. It provides evidence that feathers were present in the tyrannosauroid lineage.
summary: A small early tyrannosauroid with preserved filamentous integument. It provides evidence that feathers were present in the tyrannosauroid lineage.

discovery.body: Named by Xu et al., 2004. The record is known from the Lujiatun Unit of the Yixian Formation, Liaoning. The holotype, IVPP V14243, is a semi-articulated skeleton with an almost complete skull; IVPP V14242 and TNP01109 are referred.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype, IVPP V14243, is a semi-articulated skeleton with an almost complete skull. IVPP V14242 and TNP01109 are referred specimens; IVPP V11579 is a referred skull, not the holotype.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: The Lujiatun Unit of the Yixian Formation, Liaoning, records the species in the Early Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈126–125 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The skeleton is lightly built, the forelimbs are relatively long and three-fingered, and filamentous integument is preserved around the tail and body. The skull is almost complete.

behaviour.body: No direct evidence of social, nesting or parental behaviour. The filaments are direct evidence of a body covering, but their function is not established. The Lujiatun lake-margin setting is habitat context, not a behavioural record.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a partial skeleton with integument impressions. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The holotype is IVPP V14243, a semi-articulated skeleton with an almost complete skull from the Lujiatun Unit of the Yixian Formation. Filamentous integument is preserved. Brusatte & Carr (2016) recovered Dilong outside Proceratosauridae, so the family label is provisional; no gut contents are known.

primer.lead: Dilong paradoxus was a small, feathered [theropod](/learn/major-dinosaur-groups) from the [Early Cretaceous](/deep-time?period=cretaceous) of Liaoning, China. It is an early relative of Tyrannosaurus, but it was about the size of a large dog rather than a giant predator.
paragraphs: The best specimen preserves an almost complete skull and a lightly built skeleton. Filamentous integument is preserved around the body and tail, showing that a feather-like covering was present in this part of the tyrannosauroid family tree. The filaments are not modern flight feathers, and their function is unknown.

Its teeth indicate a meat-eating diet, but no gut contents are known. The exact family placement is debated: some analyses put Dilong outside Proceratosauridae, and others place it outside Tyrannosauroidea altogether.
primer.takeaway: A small feathered cousin of Tyrannosaurus, important for the early history of the group.
